The Gap Between Possible and Deployed

Cheaper open AI methods sit on the shelf for months—held back by hardware write-offs and quarterly calendars until automation breaks lock-in.

[Electricity < 12% of Task Cost · Switching Is the Moat]

1/3 Open methods routinely run AI far more cheaply on existing machines, yet products often wait months or years to adopt them.

2/3 Machine hardware costs far more per task than raw electricity, backed by both operating cash and circular supplier investments.

3/3 Corporate calendars delay rollouts in quarterly steps until automation tools slash switching friction and force cheaper methods into production.
